Cleavage of Oxygen-Sulfur Double Bond and Carbon-Sulfur Bond: 
Unusual Highly Selective Electrophilic Addition of Allenylic Sulfoxides 
Minyan Wang, Chunling Fu, and Shengming Ma* 
Received (in XXX, XXX) Xth XXXXXXXXX 20XX, Accepted Xth XXXXXXXXX 20XX 
DOI: 10.1039/b000000x 5 
Selective cleavage and formation of covalent bonds is an everlasting topic in science of synthesis. 
Recently, much attention has been paid to the activation and functionalization of inert covalent 
chemical bonds such as CTH, CTO, CTCl bonds, etc. In this article, we would like to report that 
hydrogen bonding may mediate an efficient and highly selective cleavage of the O=S bond and CT
S bond in 1,2Tallenyl sulfoxides with I 2 and BnSH, which transfer the oxygen to the adjacent 10 
allenylic carbon atom forming the ketone or aldehyde carbonyl functionality with one C=C bond in 
the allene moiety remained in a highly stereoselective manner. This method provides a general and 
highly stereoselective entry to the synthetically important yet difficult to prepare polyTsubstituted 
enals or enones. 
Introduction 15 
 Allenes have been continuously catching the attent ion from the 
scientists due to its broad existence in biological ly active natural 
products as well as pharmaceuticals. 1,2 In addition, the chemistry 
of allenes has also become more and more important due to the 
versatile reactivities observed with these unique t wo cumulated 20 
C=C bonds. 3T5 However, due to the presence of two C=C bonds, 
control of selectivity with the reaction to each of  the two C=C 
bonds is still challenging. For example, in all the  known 
electrophilic addition reactions, the relatively el ectronTrich C=C 
bonds are reacted as usual by following the general  principle: 25 
these is no report that in the presence of two cumu lated C=C 
bonds with different electronic properties, the ele ctronTdeficient 
C=C bonds are electrophilically reacted (Scheme 1). 6,7 On the 
other hand, although polysubstituted stereodefined α,β T
unsaturated enones or enals are important building blocks in 30 
organic synthesis, 8 however, there is no general methods for their 
synthesis due to the limited success on control the  
stereoselectivity of the C=C bond, 9T15  difficulty to introduce the 
desired substituent to the specific location(s) of these types of 
compounds, 16T18  the issue of regioselectivity, 19  and the limited 35 
access to the corresponding sterodefined allylic al cohols  (See SI 
for detailed literature information). 20T30 Herein we show the 
realization of such a highly selective electrophili c addition 
reaction with the electronTdeficient C=C bond in th e readily 
available 1,2Tallenylic sulfoxides from propargylic  alcohols, 31T34 40 
which provides a straightforward route to the notTr eadilyT
available αTiodoTα,βTunsaturated carbonyl compounds 35T37  with an 
excellent stereoselectivity. Because of the existen ce of CTI bond, 
different substituents may be easily incorporated b y transition 
metalTcatalyzed crossTcoupling reactions. 38 45

Results and discussion 
 The current study was started with our previous ob servation on 
the reaction of nonaT3,4TdienT5Tylphenyl sulfoxide 1a  with I 2 in 50 
the presence of BnSH (Scheme 2). 39 When the reaction was 
conducted with 1.5 equiv of I 2 in MeCN in the presence of 1 
equiv of BnSH at a higher temperature (40 oC), surprisingly, 
instead of the reported reductive iodohydroxylation  product 2,39  
an unknown product 3a  was formed, albeit in rather low yield. 55 
Through careful analysis of the 1H NMR, 13 C NMR, and IR 
spectra, we noticed that there is a carbonyl functi onality in this 
unknown compound. Thus, we attempted the reaction o f this 
unknown compound 3  with 2,4Tdinitrophenylhydrazine, which 
afforded a solid product 4 . The XTray single crystal diffraction 60 
study of 4  clearly showed that this new product is 4TiodononT 3T
enT5Tone in ZTconfiguration (Scheme 2), 10  indicating that the 
electronTdeficient C=C in 1a  was surprisingly reacted formally 
here. When Et 2O was used as the solvent (entry 1, Table 1), only 
2% of ZT3a was formed with 56% of the normal reductive 65 
iodohydroxylation product ET2a. The reaction in other solvents, 
such as CH 2Cl 2, DMF, CH 3NO 2, and 1,4Tdioxane etc ., afforded

 With these evidences in hand, we reasoned that the re are two 
pathways for this reaction, which are shown in Sche me 9. The 
major pathway is as follows: EtOH in the solvent ma y form a 
hydrogen bonding with the sulfinyl oxygen, which de creases the 
35 
nucleophilicity of the sulfoxide oxygen stopping th e formation of 
cyclic intermediate M5 42 and  weakens the sulfurToxygen double 
bond to facilitate the electrophilic addition with this C=C bond. 
This C=C bond reacts with I + to form the threeTmembered 
iodonium intermediate M1 , which may be easily transformed into 40 
the intermediate M2  via the 1,3Trearrangement to release the ringT
strain. Different from the known reactions, 43  the intermediate M2  
undergoes 1,3Trearrangement to form the intermediate M3 . Next, 
the intermediate M3  would afford the aldehyde or ketone 3  upon 
releasing  PhS +. The PhS + can be captured by BnSH to afford 1T45 
benzylT2Tphenyldisulfane 8, which would react with the excessive 
I2 affording 1,2Tdiphenyldisulfane  9, and 1,2Tdibenzyldisulfane 
10 .

Conclusions 10 
 In conclusion, we have developed a unique iodohydr oxylation 
of readily available 1,2Tallenylic sulfoxides in th e presence of 
BnSH forming αTiodoTα,β Tunsaturated ketones or aldehydes in 
good to excellent yields highly stereoselectively. Based on the 
mechanistic study, we believe that the hydrogenTbonding between 15 
the sulfoxide and EtOH may be responsible for the r eversed 
regioselectivity of the two C=C bonds in allenes. T he reaction 
may easily be carried in 20 mmol or 30 mmol. The CT I bonds 
provides opportunities for further synthetic elabor ation. This 
reaction will be of high interest in the scientific  community due 20 
to the potentials of the notTreadilyTavailable prod ucts and the 
interesting mechanism. Further studies including th e new 
reactivity of the sulfoxide functionality in this a rea are being 
pursued in our laboratory.
